title: Education and Industry Come Together at Intuit Connect to Prepare the Next Generation of Accountants
summary: At Intuit Connect, educators and accounting leaders explored how collaboration, AI readiness, and the Accounting Futures Program can better prepare students for accounting careers.

- Education and Industry Come Together at Intuit Connect to Prepare the Next Generation of Accountants


Every year, Intuit hosts thousands of industry leaders at Intuit Connect in Las Vegas for a three-day deep dive on the future of accounting. This year, Intuit for Education kicked off the event with the Accounting Futures Roundtable, where industry and higher education came together to explore how they can work side by side to prepare accounting students for an evolving profession. The session gathered firm leaders who are hiring new accountants and the administrators and faculty preparing those students to graduate. The takeaway was clear: it has never been more critical for the two to collaborate in supporting today’s students as they take on the new era of accounting.


**A Widening Gap, and a Program Built to Help Close It**


Across the panel discussions and breakout activities that filled the day, the prevailing theme was how to ensure academic preparation stays aligned with professional expectations amid rapid changes in the accounting industry. With AI automating many tasks that entry-level staff once handled, new accountants have the opportunity to act as client advisors, raising the bar for graduates to think strategically and show their judgment skills from day one on the job. However, that opportunity also collides with widespread talent struggles within the industry, as 73% of firm leaders say talent shortages are severely affecting their firms, and 56% say a new entry-level hire takes six or more months to become fully productive, according to[Intuit’s 2026 Accountant Technology Survey](https://www.firmofthefuture.com/news/accountant-tech-survey-2026/) .


This gap is what the Intuit for Education[Accounting Futures Program](https://www.intuit.com/solutions/education/accounting-futures/) was created to address. Intuit for Education has spent more than a decade building free financial education resources that help students develop real-world money skills and career readiness, while also supporting educators in teaching them. The Accounting Futures Program builds on that mission, offering colleges and universities free access to modern accounting curriculum that’s focused on strategic judgment and client advisory skills, in addition to industry-recognized credentials, direct connections to leading accounting professionals, and micro-internship opportunities for students. Built around a case study model that reflects the daily complexities accountants face, the curriculum helps students sharpen their critical thinking and tackle real-world challenges, going far beyond what’s achievable in textbook and traditional lecture learning environments. The program was created in collaboration with both college educators and firm owners to ensure optimal industry alignment. The roundtable was an extension of this partnership, as attendees heard directly from Utah Valley University on how they brought Accounting Futures into their classrooms and the[measurable impact](https://www.intuit.com/solutions/education/case-studies/uvu/) it’s already had.


**In Their Own Words**


The day’s discussion helped provide valuable insight into how Intuit can continue to evolve the Accounting Futures Program to better serve students, educators, and the industry as a whole. College educators had the opportunity to voice what’s working in their classrooms and where they need support, while firm leaders also had the chance to share the skills they’re most in need of among new talent, and what they think will better prepare students to walk into their firms and be successful. Here’s what attendees had to say:


“When we’re in the classroom, we can teach the technical aspects of accounting to students: debits and credits, and how to make journal entries. But what is often lacking is the ability to apply real-world circumstances to what we teach. That’s what the Accounting Futures Program can do for us. It gives them the real-world experience that firms love to see.” – **Max Chao, Senior Continuing Lecturer, Accounting at UC Irvine**


“When it comes to the Accounting Futures Program, I would tell other educators to take a look at how they could incorporate it into their course. It is sizable. You can use it as much or as little as you want and there are many ways you can incorporate it as well. So, it’s just something where you just have to take a little bit of time to determine how you want to implement it and then Intuit has a bunch of resources available to you to help you do that along the way.” – **Nikki Sharma, Accounting Lecturer at University of North Texas**


“Because we are struggling to attract students to the field, it’s really important that they understand what accounting is actually about. Having firm leaders share their real-world experience in the classroom and show students the value of an accounting career goes a long way.” – **Dr. Tanae Acolatse, Program Manager, Bachelor of Science in Accounting at Colorado State University Global**


“I am so proud to be part of the Accounting Futures Program as an Industry Advisor. Seeing the response from the educators today, saying, ‘we want to be here, we want to be in this room, and we want to be changing,’ to me made this a perfect moment to come together, give ideas, and see the UVU example of how that success happens. We have our proof that this works and I think that gives educators hope, and for me, it’s a huge bright spot as a firm owner.” – **Jan Haugo, Founder / AI Research + Curriculum Architect at SmartAccountant.ai**


“The level of disruption that’s happening across the industry right now cannot be solved by one company or organization. We have to come together and work together to solve this. And the good news is, I actually think we can really reinvigorate this industry and drive a level of prosperity that we haven’t seen for a while. My hope is that the Accounting Futures Program will help students of today be better prepared to ultimately prosper in a career in accounting.” – **Simon Williams, Vice President, Accountant and Global Partner Programs, Intuit**


“My takeaway from today is that in order for the Accounting Futures Program to be successful and help students be better prepared, it has to come down to strong collaboration between educators and industry. We really want accountants to invest time in being an Industry Advisor because not only are they giving back to the next generation, they’re really making an investment in the future of their own firms and other firms to be successful.” – **Dave Zasada, VP of Corporate Responsibility at Intuit**


**Beyond the Roundtable**


A single day brought the room together, but it’s only the beginning of the clear path ahead. Educators, firm leaders, and Intuit left as one passionate community, united by a shared commitment to reinvigorating the accounting profession, and with a defined roadmap to put that commitment into action. By bringing classroom and firm perspectives together through the Accounting Futures Program, this community can turn shared ideas into real curriculum, real connections, and real opportunities for students. Because underneath all of it is one shared focus: the student. They’re the ones trusting this community to prepare them for what’s next, as they’re not only the future of this profession but also the next generation who will one day help power thriving economies, build businesses that allow others to grow, and enable entrepreneurs to chase their dreams.


For educators and students looking to learn more about Intuit for Education and explore the Accounting Futures Program, go to:[https://www.intuit.com/solutions/education/accounting-futures/](https://www.intuit.com/solutions/education/accounting-futures/)
